n: Because God mercifully gave them this ministry of the new covenant, the apostles don’t lose heart.

f.g: We don’t give up or lose courage.

n: They reject secret, shameful tactics and never twist God’s word. Instead they openly declare the truth and let every conscience judge them before God.

f.w: handling the word of God deceitfully

n: If the gospel seems hidden, it is hidden only from those who are perishing.

f.w: hid to them that are lost

n: Satan — “the god of this world” — has blinded unbelievers so they can’t see the light of the gospel of Christ, who perfectly shows us what God is like.

f.g: Satan, the false ruler of this fallen age.

n: The apostles preach Christ as Lord, not themselves; they present themselves as the saints’ servants for Jesus’ sake.
The God who said “Let there be light” at creation has shone into their hearts, revealing His glory in the face of Jesus Christ.

f.w: commanded the light to shine out of darkness
in the face of Jesus Christ

n: This treasure is held in fragile clay jars — ordinary, weak mortals — so it is clear the extraordinary power comes from God.

f.g: Cheap clay pots, used in that era to store valuables.

n: Pressed from every side, but not crushed; confused, but not hopeless.

f.g: At a loss, but not utterly at a loss — a wordplay in Greek.

n: Hunted, but never abandoned by God; knocked down, but not knocked out.
They carry Jesus’ dying in their bodies through constant danger and suffering, so that His life is also displayed in them.

f.w: the dying of the Lord Jesus

n: They are always being handed over to death for Jesus, so His life can be shown in their mortal bodies.
Their suffering brings spiritual life to the Corinthians.

f.w: death worketh in us, but life in you
f.g: The apostles’ sacrifices produce life in those they serve.

n: Like the psalmist who said, “I believed, therefore I spoke,” they have that same faith, so they speak.

f.w: I believed, and therefore have I spoken

n: They know God, who raised Jesus, will raise them too and present them together with the Corinthians.
Everything is for the saints’ benefit, so that as grace reaches more people, thanksgiving multiplies to God’s glory.
So they don’t lose heart. Though their bodies are wearing out, their inner selves are renewed every day.

f.w: the inward man is renewed day by day

n: Present troubles are light and brief compared with the overwhelming, eternal glory they are preparing.

f.w: light affliction, which is but for a moment

f.g: In Hebrew, “glory” (kavod) also suggests weight or heaviness — a nice contrast with “light” affliction.

n: So they focus not on what is seen but on the unseen. The visible is temporary; the unseen is eternal.

f.g: Temporary, lasting only for a time.
